name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The R288W substitution removes the positively charged guanidinium of Arg288, which lines the phosphotyrosine-binding pocket of the BTK SH2 domain. Without it, the SH2 domain cannot engage the phosphotyrosine motif of partner proteins, so the mutant fails to recruit BTK to its signalling partners.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E15", "E3", "E5", "E4", "E10", "E11", "E1", "E2"], "would_refute": "A model of a phosphotyrosine peptide docked into the SH2 pocket (built from 6HTF or 2GE9 geometry, or from AF-Q06187-F1) places Arg288 more than about 4.5 \u00c5 from the phosphate group, or the W288 model keeps peptide docking energy and contacts equal to wild type. Refutation also follows if ligand-bound SH2 structures show no pY-pocket contact at residue 288.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E15 is the only retrieved assay that tests R288 directly, and it links this pocket to a more than 200-fold loss of phosphopeptide binding. It is a combined R288/R307 mutant result on an isolated SH2 domain with synthetic peptides, so attribution to R288 alone is uncertain. E10 and E11 show no non-solvent ligand, so no pocket-bound ligand is observed; this does not refute the mechanism but leaves the pocket geometry unverified. Missing: a separate R288W binding measurement, a pY-peptide complex containing this residue, and full-length or cellular data (G5)."}

arguments: {"statement": "The Arg-to-Trp change in the SH2 helix (288-298) disrupts local packing and salt-bridge networks, so the SH2 domain misfolds or becomes less stable, which reduces expression or folding of the full-length kinase.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E4", "E13", "E6", "E7", "E8", "E9", "E3", "E1", "E12"], "would_refute": "Predicted stability change for R288W (for example FoldX or ESM-based \u0394\u0394G) is within about \u00b11 kcal/mol of wild type, the AF-Q06187-F1 helix 288-298 keeps its pLDDT and backbone geometry, and Arg288 is solvent-exposed with no buried partner in 6HTF or 2GE9. Refutation also follows if the variant's side chain makes no intra-domain contact in the experimental structures.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "The predictors (E6, E8, E9) and conservation (E7) all point to damage, but they score pathogenicity without naming a mechanism. E4 places residue 288 in a helix that is experimentally supported, which gives a plausible route to destabilisation. No retrieved study measures folding or stability of R288W (G4), and the one binding study is on the wild-type SH2 domain. This leaves stability as a plausible second explanation with no direct test yet."}
